title: Linear model and gradient descent

wrong.sum_not_mean.py: gradient is not divided by N (fails the finite-difference check)
wrong.missing_transpose.py: uses X instead of X.T in the gradient (shape error)
wrong.fit_warm_start.py: fit starts from random-looking nonzero weights/ignores zero init: history[0] is not the loss at w = 0
wrong.fit_history_after.py: history records the loss after each step, so history[0] is not the starting loss
wrong.r2_uses_mean_of_pred.py: r2_score centres on the prediction mean instead of the truth mean (overstates a biased model)
wrong.r2_no_constant_guard.py: r2_score divides by zero on a constant target

hints: Write the loss as a residual first: r = X @ w - y. Both the loss and the gradient are built from r.
dL/dw = (2/N) * X.T @ r. If your gradient has shape (N,) instead of (D,), you used X where X.T belongs. fit is just a loop: start at zeros, record the loss, then step.
r2_score = 1 - sum((y - y_hat)^2) / sum((y - mean(y))^2). Centre on the mean of the TRUTH. Watch the constant-target case, where the denominator is zero.
